This report filed by the Special Commissioner, Sabarimala, pursuant to the directions contained in the order of this Court dated 20.01.2023 in SSCR No.23 of 2022, is regarding crowd management and other aspects at Sabarimala in connection with Mandala- Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25).
2. On 12.11.2024, when this SSCR came up for consideration, the learned Senior Government Pleader has made available for the perusal of this Court, in a sealed cover, the Police Bandobast Scheme in connection with Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25). We have perused the same and returned it to the learned Senior Government Pleader, in a sealed cover. By the order dated 12.11.2024, this Court ordered that it is for the respondents herein to comply with,
in letter and spirit, the general directions contained in the order of this Court dated 20.01.2023 during the Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024- 25) in order to ensure that the pilgrims have a safe and comfortable pilgrimage during the festival season. Paragraph 14 of the order of this Court dated 12.11.2024 reads thus;. 
"14. In Suo Motu v. State of Kerala and others [2023 (4) KHC SN 11] - order dated 20.01.2023 in SSCR 23 of 2022 and DBP No.70 of 2022 - this Court issued various directions regarding (i) Police Bandobast Scheme for Mandala- Makaravilakku festival season [Para.15.4], (ii) Facilities by the Forest Department in the traditional trekking path [Para.16.5],
(iii) Fixation price of food items in the eateries [Para.19.1], (iv) Annadhanam at Sabarimala, Pamba and Nilakkal [Para.20.2],
(v) Crowd Management at Pamba and Sannidhanam [Para.22.5], (vi) Crowd and vehicle management at Nilakkal [Para.23.1], (vii) KSRTC buses for Sabarimala Pilgrims and Nilakkal-Pamba Chain Service [Para.25.6], (viii) Entry of Vehicles from Nilakkal and parking of vehicles at Pamba [Para.28.4]. By the order dated 20.01.2023, SSCR 23 of 2022 and DBP No.70 of 2022 were disposed of by directing that the directions contained therein are complied with, in letter and spirit, by all concerned, during Mandala-Makaravilakku festival seasons. It is for the respondents herein to comply with, in letter and spirit, the general directions contained in the order of this Court dated 20.01.2023 during the Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25) in order to ensure that the pilgrims have a safe and comfortable pilgrimage during the festival season."

4 3. Today, when this matter is taken up for consideration, the learned Senior Government Pleader has made available for the perusal of this Court, a report dated 13.11.2024 of the 14th respondent Chief Police Co-ordinator [Additional Director General of Police (Police Headquarters)],
Sabarimala, which is being filed today along with a memo, regarding crowd management with specific reference to the Police Bandobast Scheme during Mandala- Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25).
4. Police Bandobast Scheme for Mandala- Makaravilakku festival season:- The Kerala Police has already prepared a detailed Police Bandobast Scheme, deploying police officers/personnel under the direct supervision of an officer of the rank of Additional Director General of Police, who is appointed as the Chief Police Co-ordinator, who is assisted by a Joint Police Co- ordinator in the rank of Inspector General of Police and three Additional Police Co-ordinators in the rank of Deputy Inspector General of Police. 
4.1. The Police Bandobast Scheme divides responsibilities into two parts: Part A for pilgrim facilitation and management and Part B for crisis management. The entire route from Nilakkal to Sannidhanam has been divided into three sectors. Other areas of Pathanamthitta district are included in the fourth sector. Several divisions have been created under each sector for effective crowd management. The responsibility of each sector is assigned to an officer of the rank of Superintendent of Police, as Special Officer. Under the Special Officers, Joint Special Officers of the rank of Assistant Superintendents of Police and Assistant Special Officers of the rank of Additional Superintendents of Police are appointed. Each division is supervised by an officer of the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police. The Controlling Officers are assigned duties based on their expertise and experience. 
4.2. A total number of 13,665 police officials will be deployed for Sabarimala duty in six phases. 
Bomb Detection and Disposal Squads equipped with Metal detectors and X-ray scanners are also being deployed. One company of RAF and two teams of NDRF are also being deployed for duty for the entire season. 
4.3. A multifaceted Edathavalams Bandobast Scheme incorporating all Sabarimala Edathavalams in Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Alappuzha and Idukki districts is being implemented to provide a systematic security and assistance framework. District Traffic Regulation Scheme is in place at Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki and Kollam districts to streamline vehicle flow and aid pilgrims during the pilgrimage season. A continuous Drone Surveillance System has also been included for the entire pilgrimage season. 
4.4. Having considered the submissions made at the Bar, we deem it appropriate to direct the 2nd respondent State Police Chief and the 14th respondent Chief Police Co-ordinator, Sabarimala,
through the Special Officers, the Joint Special Officers, the Assistant Special Officers and the Controlling Officers, to ensure proper crowd management in Sabarimala during Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25) to facilitate safe, secure, smooth and hassle-free darshan for all the pilgrims.

5 5. Annadhanam at Sabarimala Sannidhanam, Pamba and Nilakkal:- The learned Standing Counsel for the Travancore Devaswom Board would submit that the Board will provide Annadhanam to pilgrims throughout the day at Sabarimala Sannidhanam, Pamba and Nilakkal. 
5.1. The learned Standing Counsel for Travancore Devaswom Board would submit that the Board has constructed an Annadanam Hall at Sannidhanam with more than 1,40,000sq.ft. area, with a seating facility for 2,000 pilgrims at a time. The Board has made all arrangements for providing Annadanam to pilgrims throughout the day. Breakfast, lunch and supper will be given to the pilgrims throughout the day. Annadanam will be provided day and night continuously, with a short intermittent break of 30 minutes for cleaning and arranging the hall and the tables. A sufficient number of workers and staff are being arranged for the preparation and distribution of food. A Special Officer has been appointed in Sannidhanam for the conduct of Annadanam efficiently and without giving room for any complaint. Upma and Kadala, Chukkukappi and Chukkuvellam will be given for breakfast in the morning from 6.00 a.m. onwards. Meals with Ponni rice, Sambar, Aviyal,
Thoran and Pickle/Vegetable Pulav, Salad and Pickle will be given for lunch from 12.00 noon onwards. Kuthari Kanji, Cherupayar curry and Pickle/Upma and Kadala will be given for supper in the evening from 6.00 p.m. onwards till the last person leaves Sannidhanam. The Board has also constructed a two-storied Annadanam Hall at Pampa, which has the capacity to provide food for 500 pilgrims at a time. Annadanam Hall at Nilakkal has the capacity to provide food for 200 pilgrims at a time. The same dishes are being given in Pampa and Nilakkal. The Board has also made arrangements to provide a sufficient quantity of drinking water and 'Chukkuvellam' to the pilgrims at Annadanam halls and also at different points throughout the trekking path from Pamba to Sannidhanam. 
5.2. Having considered submissions made at the Bar, we deem it appropriate to direct the Travancore Devaswom Board to make necessary arrangements to provide Annadanam to pilgrims throughout the day during Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25) in the Annadanam halls at Sannidhanam, Pamba and Nilakkal. The Assistant Executive Officer,
Sabarimala, who is in the rank of Assistant Devaswom Commissioner, shall monitor the entire activities relating to Annadanam at Sannidhanam and the Administrative Officers at Pamba and Nilakkal shall monitor the entire activities relating to Annadanam at Pamba and Nilakkal. The pilgrims shall be informed, at regular intervals, through the public address system, about Annadanam at Sannidhanam, Pamba and Nilakkal. 
5.3. The officers in the Vigilance Wing of the Travancore Devaswom Board and the Executive Magistrates at Sannidhanam, Pamba and Nilakkal and also the Executive Magistrate in the office of the Special Commissioner, Sabarimala shall conduct regular inspections in the Annadanam halls at Sannidhanam, Pamba and Nilakkal and any shortfall in the conduct of Annadanam shall be reported to the Devaswom Commissioner and also to the Special Commissioner, Sabarimala, who shall bring it to the notice of this Court for immediate interference. 
6. KSRTC buses for Sabarimala Pilgrims and Nilakkal- Pamba Chain Service:- By the orders of this Court in SSCR No.23 of 2022, the 7th respondent Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) was directed to provide sufficient number of buses for Nilakkal-Pamba chain service,
Suo Motu vs State Of Kerala on 14 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157192600/
6 during Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1199ME (2023-24). The Executive Engineer,
Sabarimala Development Project was directed to install temporary CCTV cameras in the boarding points at Nilakkal and Pamba, in order to ensure that the vehicles used by KSRTC for Nilakkal-Pamba chain service are carrying only passengers within the permissible limit, as per permit conditions, and also to ensure the availability of a sufficient number of vehicles in the boarding points at Nilakkal and Pamba. It was ordered that any shortfall in Nilakkal-Pamba chain service by KSRTC shall be brought to the notice of the Special Commissioner, Sabarimala, who shall file reports before this Court seeking appropriate directions. 
6.1. By the orders of this Court in SSCR No.23 of 2022, the Police and the Enforcement Wing of the Motor Vehicles Department were directed to have a constant vigil on the movement of pilgrims in Nilakkal-Pamba chain service by KSRTC. Temporary CCTV cameras were provided at the boarding points of KSRTC at Nilakkal and Pamba (9 at Nilakkal and 12 at Pamba), which were being monitored in the Police Control Rooms at Nilakkal and Pamba. By the order dated 23.12.2022, this Court directed the Enforcement Wing of the Motor Vehicles Department to take necessary steps to ensure that the operation of buses by KSRTC for the movement of pilgrims is strictly in compliance with the directions contained in the orders of this Court in SSCR No.23 of 2022 and also the orders in SSCR No.20 of 2021 and that, all vehicles have valid Fitness Certificates. This Court directed the 3rd respondent District Police Chief, Pathanamthitta and the 4th respondent District Collector,
Pathanamthitta to make proper arrangements, in consultation with the concerned officer of the Travancore Devaswom Board and also the Special Commissioner, Sabarimala, to avoid congestion of pilgrims at the boarding points of KSRTC chain service at Thriveni-Pamba and Nilakkal. 
6.2. The learned Standing Counsel for KSRTC seeks time to get instructions on the arrangements made by KSRTC regarding Nilakkal- Pamba chain service. 
6.3. The learned Standing Counsel for Travancore Devaswom Board would submit that temporary CCTV cameras are provided at the boarding points of KSRTC at Nilakkal and Pamba, as done during the previous Mandala-Makaravilakku festival seasons, for being monitored in the Police Control Rooms at Nilakkal and Pamba. 
6.4. Having considered the submissions made at the Bar, we deem it appropriate to direct the 3rd respondent District Police Chief, Pathanamthitta and the 4th respondent District Collector,
Pathanamthitta to take necessary steps to ensure the availability of a sufficient number of KSRTC buses for Nilakkal-Pamba chain service, in the boarding points at Nilakkal and Pamba and to avoid congestion of pilgrims at the boarding points of KSRTC chain service at Thriveni- Pamba and Nilakkal, during Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25). The Police shall ensure that senior citizens, persons with disabilities and children of tender age are permitted entry through the front door of the buses used for Nilakkal-Pamba chain service, to the extent possible,
before the entry of others. The Police shall take special care in the case of children of tender age. 
6.5. Through temporary CCTV cameras installed in the boarding points at Nilakkal and Pamba,
which are being monitored in the Police Control Rooms at Nilakkal and Pamba, the Police shall ensure that the vehicles used by KSRTC for Nilakkal-Pamba chain service carry only passengers Suo Motu vs State Of Kerala on 14 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157192600/
7 within the permissible limit, as per permit conditions. The additional 17th respondent Transport Commissioner, through the Enforcement Officers of the Motor Vehicles Department, shall ensure that all vehicles used for Nilakkal- Pamba chain service have valid Fitness Certificates. 
7. Facilities by the Forest Department in the traditional trekking path:- The learned Senior Government Pleader, on instructions, would submit that the Forest Officials under the 5th respondent Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (Wildlife) and Chief Wildlife Warden has already taken various measures to provide adequate facilities to Sabarimala pilgrims trekking through the traditional path, during Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25). The additional 15th respondent District Collector, Idukki has issued orders regulating the movement of pilgrims through the traditional trekking path. 
7.1. The restrictions imposed on the movement of pilgrims through the traditional trekking path from Erumeli were under challenge in W.P.(C)No.40899 of 2022. In the said writ petition the petitioners have sought for a writ of mandamus commanding respondents 5 to 8 therein not to impose any restriction on the movement of devotees on the traditional trekking path from Erumeli,
without consultation with Malayarayan tribal community and adversely affecting the traditional religious practices of that community and other devotees, or divert pilgrims to non-traditional paths to Sabarimala Temple, which is more onerous or restrictive than the restrictions on the two non-traditional paths. They have also sought for a writ of mandamus commanding respondents 1 to 4 therein to draw up a master plan for the protection and maintenance of Erumeli-Sannidhanam traditional path with due right of administration to the members of Malayarayan community and other communities, to maintain and protect the places of worship on that traditional path; and a writ of mandamus commanding the respondents therein to protect the rites, rituals and beliefs of the petitioners and members of Malayarayan tribal community, without imposing any illegal and unreasonable restrictions, on the movement of devotees to Sabarimala Temple through the traditional trekking path from Erumeli. 
7.2. On 16.12.2022, when that writ petition came up for admission, the learned Senior Government Pleader, on instructions, from the concerned Forest officials and also the District Police Chief,
Idukki, submitted that restrictions have been imposed in the movement of pilgrims through the traditional trekking path mainly on account of the fact that the said path through Periyar Tiger Reserve, was not being used for the last more than two years. On 22.12.2022, during the course of arguments, the learned Senior Government Pleader made available for the perusal of this Court, the route map of the traditional trekking path from Erumeli to Pamba, prepared by the Kerala Forest and Wildlife Department, marking the camera points, camp-sheds, the places where elephant squads are deployed and the locations of emergency medical centre and the health centre with doctor. 
7.3. By the judgment dated 22.12.2022 - C.N. Madhusoodanan and another v. State of Kerala and others [2022:Ker:75522] this Court dismissed W.P.(C)No.40899 of 2022 holding that the restrictions regarding movement of Sabarimala pilgrims through the traditional trekking path, by fixing timings as per the order dated 25.11.2022 of the District Collector, Idukki, has been made in order to ensure the safety of pilgrims, which warrants no interference. Therefore, the request made Suo Motu vs State Of Kerala on 14 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157192600/
8 by the petitioners in that writ petition to open up the traditional trekking path from Erumeli round the clock without any time restriction stands rejected. This Court held further that when the traditional trekking path is through Periyar Tiger Reserve, where passage of wild animals is on the higher side during night time, entry of pilgrims during Mandala- Makaravilakku festival season has to be regulated in an appropriate manner. When Periyar Tiger Reserve is a protected area, it has to be preserved as such. Therefore, this Court found that the request made by the petitioners for drawing up a master plan for the traditional trekking path, as sought for in that writ petition,
deserves no consideration. 
7.4. Having considered the submissions made at the Bar, we deem it appropriate to direct the 5th respondent Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (Wildlife) and Chief Wildlife Warden to ensure,
through the concerned Forest Officials, that adequate facilities are provided to Sabarimala pilgrims in the traditional trekking path from Erumeli and also at 8 Thavalams along that route, where 'viri'
facility is provided to the pilgrims, during Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25), in order to ensure safe and secure movement of pilgrims through that trekking path. The movement of pilgrims through the trekking path during Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25) shall be regulated by the orders of the additional 15th respondent District Collector, Idukki, fixing the timings, depending upon the number of pilgrims. 
8. Fixation price of food items in the eateries:- The learned Senior Government Pleader would submit that the 4th respondent District Collector, Pathanamthitta has already issued a notification fixing the price of food items in the eateries in Pathanamthitta during Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25).
8.1. In Karthigesu K. and others v. State of Kerala and others [2015 (3) KHC 323] a Division Bench of this Court held that the said judgment, whereby the price lists published by the District Collector,
Pathanamthitta, fixing the price of various food stuffs in the hotels and restaurants in Pathanamthitta District during Sabarimala pilgrimage season 2013-14 and 2014-15 was set aside,
will not stand in the way of the District Collector, Pathanamthitta or the Travancore Devaswom Board from fixing the price of food stuffs in the hotels and restaurants in Sabarimala, Pamba, etc.,
which are temporarily put up during each pilgrimage season, on the strength of the permission/licence granted by the Board. 
8.3. Having considered the submissions made at the Bar, we deem it appropriate to direct all concerned to ensure strict compliance of the notification issued by the 4th respondent District Collector, Pathanamthitta fixing the prices of food stuff in the eateries Pathanamthitta district,
including hotels, light refreshment stalls, etc. at Sabarimala, Pamba and Nilakkal, opened during Mandala- Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25), on the strength of the permission/licence granted by the Travancore Devaswom Board. Taking into account the fact that a large number of pilgrims from North India and neighbouring States of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh visit Sabarimala during every pilgrimage season, the District Administration/Enforcement Officers exercising the powers under the Kerala Food Stuffs (Display of Prices by Catering Establishments) Order, 1977 shall insist on display of price list of food stuffs in all eateries in Sabarimala, Pamba and Nilakkal in English, Hindi, Kannada and Telugu, in addition Suo Motu vs State Of Kerala on 14 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157192600/
9 to Malayalam. The Enforcement Wing of the Food Safety Department shall conduct periodical inspections at the eateries during Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25). 
The officers in the Vigilance Wing of the Travancore Devaswom Board and the Executive Magistrates at Sannidhanam, Pamba and Nilakkal and also the Executive Magistrate in the office of the Special Commissioner, Sabarimala shall conduct regular inspections in all eateries to ensure that the pilgrims are not being exploited by the traders by collecting excess price for food stuffs. 
9. Crowd Management at Pamba and Sannidhanam:- In terms of the order of this Court in Suo Motu v. Travancore Devaswom Board and others [2022 (7) KHC SN 5], verification of Virtual-Q tickets and other related matters are the responsibilities of the Kerala Police, as part of crowd management. For effective crowd management during festival seasons and also Maasapoojas the Kerala Police should have access to the database in Virtual-Q system. When specific threat inputs have been received in respect of Sabarimala Temple, the Kerala Police will have to take preventive action after screening and verifying the database. 
9.1. In various orders passed by this Court in SSCR No.23 0f 2022, it was made clear that, the Police shall take special care in the case of aged persons, persons with disabilities and also minor children. 
By the order dated 16.12.2022 in that SSCR this Court directed the Travancore Devaswom Board to introduce a special queue in the Nadapanthal at Sabarimala Sannidhanam for senior citizens,
persons with disabilities, children below the age of 10 years and also persons having health issues. It was also ordered that a place shall be earmarked at Sannidhanam, where persons in the special queue can wait for their group members and that the information about the waiting place shall be made known to the pilgrims through the public address system. 
9.2. Having considered the submissions made at the Bar, we deem it appropriate to direct the Travancore Devaswom Board to continue the special queue in the Nadapanthal at Sabarimala Sannidhanam for senior citizens, persons with disabilities, children below the age of 10 years and also persons having health issues in terms of the directions contained in the orders issued in SSCR No.23 of 2022, during Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25). The 14th respondent Chief Police Co-ordinator, the Joint Police Co-ordinator and the Additional Police Coordinators at Sannidhanam, Pamba and Nilakkal shall regulate crowd management at Sabarimala in an appropriate manner, in order to ensure that all the devotees have a comfortable darshan at Sannidhanam. When the tail end of the queue is beyond the Nadappanthal at Sannidhanam, the Police shall regulate the movement of pilgrims through Pathinettampadi, in an appropriate manner,
to ensure that it reaches the bench-mark fixed with reference to the number of pilgrims per hour,
subject to special care for aged persons, persons with disability and children below the age of 10 years. The 2nd respondent State Police Chief and the 14th respondent Chief Police Co-ordinator,
Sabarimala shall ensure that only experienced Police personnel are posted at Pathinettampadi to support the pilgrims while the pilgrims climb Pathinettampadi. Police shall take special care in the case of children of tender age, persons with disabilities and senior citizens. 
9.3. The Police shall monitor crowd management in Sabarimala at regular intervals and take appropriate measures, in consultation with the District Collector, Pathanamthitta, the Travancore Devaswom Board and also the Special Commissioner, Sabarimala, in order to maintain the optimal Suo Motu vs State Of Kerala on 14 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157192600/
10 and safe position for the tail end of the queue at the end of queue complex in Saramkuthy and Marakkoottam sector, so that Marakkottam X-Cross junction is kept congestion free for outflow of pilgrims, ambulance service and other emergency services. 
10. Crowd and vehicle management at Nilakkal:- As stated in the report of the 14th respondent Chief Police Co-ordinator, Sabarimala, during rush hours, the vehicle flow at Nilakkal is managed by 'hold and release' mechanism. If at any point of time, the crowd and vehicle holding capacity of Nilakkal is exhausted, vehicles carrying pilgrims will be halted at Edathavalams and other identified parking grounds enroute, in coordination with the District Police Chiefs concerned. A hold and release mechanism will be maintained at Edathavalams for effective vehicle management. 
10.1. Having considered the submissions made at the Bar, we deem it appropriate to direct the 2nd respondent State Police Chief, the 14th respondent Chief Police Co-ordinator, Sabarimala, the 3rd respondent District Police Chief, Pathanamthitta and the 4 th respondent District Collector,
Pathanamthitta to manage the vehicle flow at Nilakkal by 'hold and release' mechanism, during Mandala- Makaravilakku festival season of 1200 ME (2024-25) by halting the vehicles carrying pilgrims at Edathavalams and other identified parking grounds enroute, in coordination with the District Police Chiefs and the District Collectors concerned. The management of vehicle flow at Nilakkal through 'hold and release' mechanism shall be informed to the Executive Officer Sabarimala and also the Special Commissioner, Sabarimala, which shall also be announced through the public address system at Sannidhanam, Nilakkal and Pamba, for the information of the pilgrims. 
11. The learned Standing Counsel for the Travancore Devaswom Board would submit, as permitted by the Tantri, Darshan time has already been increased to 18 hours per day. The learned Standing Counsel seeks time to file a report by the Secretary of the Board on the decisions taken regarding Virtual-Q booking and spot booking. The learned Standing Counsel would point out that the Board has already made arrangements to distribute 'Chukkuvellam' and biscuits to the pilgrims round the clock. 
12. The learned Standing Counsel for the 8th respondent Kerala Water Authority would submit that the Water Authority has already made necessary arrangements at Nilakkal and Pamba to ensure uninterrupted water supply to pilgrims during Mandala- Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25). The additional 15th respondent Superintending Engineer, Pathanamthitta shall supervise all the activities of the Water Authority in this regard.

Police Bandobast Scheme for Mandala- Makaravilakku festival season:-

The Kerala Police has already prepared a detailed Police Bandobast Scheme, deploying police officers/personnel under the direct supervision of an officer of the rank of Additional Director General of Police, who is appointed as the Chief Police Co-ordinator, who is assisted by a Joint Police Co- ordinator in the rank of Inspector General of Police and three Additional Police Co-ordinators in the rank of Deputy Inspector General of Police.
4.1. The Police Bandobast Scheme divides responsibilities into two parts: Part A for pilgrim facilitation and management and Part B for crisis management.
The entire route from Nilakkal to Sannidhanam has been divided into three sectors.
Other areas of Pathanamthitta district are included in the fourth sector.
Several divisions have been created under each sector for effective crowd management.
The responsibility of each sector is assigned to an officer of the rank of Superintendent of Police, as Special Officer.
Under the Special Officers, Joint Special Officers of the rank of Assistant Superintendents of Police and Assistant Special Officers of the rank of Additional Superintendents of Police are appointed.
Each division is supervised by an officer of the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police.
The Controlling Officers are assigned duties based on their expertise and experience.
4.2. A total number of 13,665 police officials will be deployed for Sabarimala duty in six phases.
Bomb Detection and Disposal Squads equipped with Metal detectors and X-ray scanners are also being deployed.
One company of RAF and two teams of NDRF are also being deployed for duty for the entire season.

4.3. A multifaceted Edathavalams Bandobast Scheme incorporating all Sabarimala Edathavalams in Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Alappuzha and Idukki districts is being implemented to provide a systematic security and assistance framework.
District Traffic Regulation Scheme is in place at Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki and Kollam districts to streamline vehicle flow and aid pilgrims during the pilgrimage season.
A continuous Drone Surveillance System has also been included for the entire pilgrimage season.

A Special Officer has been appointed in Sannidhanam for the conduct of Annadanam efficiently and without giving room for any complaint.

7. Facilities by the Forest Department in the traditional trekking path:-

The learned Senior Government Pleader, on instructions, would submit that the Forest Officials under the 5th respondent Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (Wildlife) and Chief Wildlife Warden has already taken various measures to provide adequate facilities to Sabarimala pilgrims trekking through the traditional path, during Mandala-Makaravilakku festival season of 1200ME (2024-25).
The additional 15th respondent District Collector, Idukki has issued orders regulating the movement of pilgrims through the traditional trekking path.
7.1. The restrictions imposed on the movement of pilgrims through the traditional trekking path from Erumeli were under challenge in W.P.(C)No.40899 of 2022.

In the said writ petition the petitioners have sought for a writ of mandamus commanding respondents 5 to 8 therein not to impose any restriction on the movement of devotees on the traditional trekking path from Erumeli,
without consultation with Malayarayan tribal community and adversely affecting the traditional religious practices of that community and other devotees, or divert pilgrims to non-traditional paths to Sabarimala Temple, which is more onerous or restrictive than the restrictions on the two non-traditional paths.

They have also sought for a writ of mandamus commanding respondents 1 to 4 therein to draw up a master plan for the protection and maintenance of Erumeli-Sannidhanam traditional path with due right of administration to the members of Malayarayan community and other communities, to maintain and protect the places of worship on that traditional path; and a writ of mandamus commanding the respondents therein to protect the rites, rituals and beliefs of the petitioners and members of Malayarayan tribal community, without imposing any illegal and unreasonable restrictions, on the movement of devotees to Sabarimala Temple through the traditional trekking path from Erumeli.

7.2. On 16.12.2022, when that writ petition came up for admission, the learned Senior Government Pleader, on instructions, from the concerned Forest officials and also the District Police Chief,
Idukki, submitted that restrictions have been imposed in the movement of pilgrims through the traditional trekking path mainly on account of the fact that the said path through Periyar Tiger Reserve, was not being used for the last more than two years.

On 22.12.2022, during the course of arguments, the learned Senior Government Pleader made available for the perusal of this Court, the route map of the traditional trekking path from Erumeli to Pamba, prepared by the Kerala Forest and Wildlife Department, marking the camera points, camp-sheds, the places where elephant squads are deployed and the locations of emergency medical centre and the health centre with doctor.

7.3. By the judgment dated 22.12.2022 - C.N. Madhusoodanan and another v. State of Kerala and others [2022:Ker:75522] this Court dismissed W.P.(C)No.40899 of 2022 holding that the restrictions regarding movement of Sabarimala pilgrims through the traditional trekking path, by fixing timings as per the order dated 25.11.2022 of the District Collector, Idukki, has been made in order to ensure the safety of pilgrims, which warrants no interference.
